S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

info.persona: Alfred Miller blends hands‑on ingenuity, community spirit, and a steady curiosity, turning each bolt, brew, and garden harvest into a practical lesson in sharing and improvement.
info.professional_persona: Alfred Miller, a seasoned electrician with deep proficiency in residential and commercial wiring, NEC compliance, and solar photovoltaic installation, channels their curiosity and practicality into leading small crews, mentoring apprentices, and pursuing a Master Electrician certification and contractor’s license to launch a family‑run electrical services business focused on renewable energy and home‑automation solutions.
info.cultural_background: Alfred grew up in the Bluegrass region of Kentucky, raised in a modest, white, middle‑class family with German and Anglo‑American roots. His upbringing emphasized Southern hospitality, a strong work ethic, and community involvement. He attended local public schools and later pursued some college-level coursework at Northern Kentucky Community and Technical College in electrical technology. Family traditions—such as celebrating the Kentucky Derby, holding Thanksgiving and Christmas gatherings with homemade Southern dishes, and participating in church and local fairs—have shaped his values. Alfred’s cultural identity blends Appalachian folk music appreciation, a love for outdoor recreation, and a devotion to practical craftsmanship, all of which inform both his professional life and personal pursuits.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Alfred enjoys a blend of hands‑on and outdoor activities that reflect his curiosity and love for community. He spends weekends fishing and hiking in the nearby parks, works on woodworking projects that let him craft furniture for his home, and experiments with home‑brewing craft beer. His practical side shows in DIY electronics projects using Arduino and Raspberry Pi, while his social side shines through family barbecues, volunteering at his church, and attending local country and bluegrass concerts. He also tends a modest vegetable garden and occasionally helps friends restore classic cars.
info.sports_persona: Alfred Miller avidly supports the Cincinnati Bengals and Cincinnati Reds, participates in a local weekend hiking and trail‑running club, and plays second base on a community softball league that meets at the neighborhood park after Sunday barbecues.
info.arts_persona: Alfred Miller enjoys country and bluegrass concerts, frequently listening to Ricky Skaggs and Sturgill Simpson, while also appreciating the folk paintings of local artist Sarah Franks and attending occasional stage productions at the Actors’ Theatre of Louisville.
info.travel_persona: Alfred Miller delights in weekend road trips across Kentucky’s rolling hills, has explored Nashville’s music scene and the Grand Canyon’s vistas, and dreams of touring Germany’s solar farms and hiking Norway’s fjords on a future vacation.
info.culinary_persona: Alfred Miller favors smoky brisket, hickory‑infused home‑brewed IPA, fresh garden tomatoes tossed with olive oil and basil, and classic cornbread, often crafting wood‑fired pizza topped with locally sourced peppers and cheese for family barbecues.

info.persona: Martha Johnston is a disciplined, curiosity‑driven physicist who balances rigorous research with mountain hikes, piano practice, and a competitive love of puzzles, all while wrestling with perfectionism, occasional stress‑induced migraines, and an unrelenting quest for both scientific and personal excellence.
info.professional_persona: Martha Johnston, a condensed matter physicist and optical spectroscopist, leverages meticulous experimental design, Python and MATLAB programming, and their philosophical training to lead precise, high‑impact research projects, while their disciplined, organized nature and competitive drive push them to secure major grants and mentor graduate students with an exacting yet supportive laboratory culture.
info.cultural_background: Martha was born and raised in the Seattle metropolitan area, growing up in a suburban neighborhood in Bellevue. Her family, of European descent, emphasized education, self‑reliance, and civic responsibility, values that align with the broader Pacific Northwest culture of environmental stewardship and progressive social outlook. She participates in the region’s vibrant arts scene—frequenting local galleries, attending literary readings, and supporting the city’s renowned coffee culture. Martha’s Scandinavian‑influenced upbringing instilled an appreciation for modesty and practicality, while her humanities education deepened her awareness of cultural histories, including the indigenous peoples of the area. She identifies with a multicultural, inclusive community that values scientific inquiry, sustainability, and artistic expression.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her off‑hours, Martha finds balance in the natural surroundings of the Pacific Northwest. She regularly hikes the Cascades, often combining the trek with landscape photography that captures the region’s misty forests and alpine vistas. An avid pianist, she practices classical repertoire and occasionally experiments with contemporary compositions, using music as a structured yet expressive outlet. She is an enthusiastic reader, gravitating toward British literature, modern novels, and nonfiction works on the philosophy of science and epistemology. To manage stress, she practices yoga and mindfulness meditation, and she enjoys solving puzzles—crosswords, Sudoku, and strategic board games like Go—that satisfy her competitive streak. Martha also cultivates a small herb garden on her balcony and explores cooking, especially Southeast Asian dishes, which she refines through meticulous recipe testing.
info.sports_persona: Martha Johnston fuels their fitness through seasonal hikes in the Cascades with the Seattle Alpine Club, supports the Seattle Seahawks in football, the Seattle Sounders FC in soccer, and follows the Portland Trail Blazers in basketball, while their analytical mindset translates into a methodical approach to trail planning and a competitive spirit in local Go tournaments.
info.arts_persona: Martha Johnston expresses creativity as an avid pianist performing works by Beethoven, Rachmaninoff, and contemporary composer Philip Glass, while their love of British literature leads them to reread Virginia Woolf and modern novels by Kazuo Ishiguro, and they regularly attend performances by the Seattle Symphony and exhibitions at the Seattle Art Museum featuring artists like Yayoi Kusama.
info.travel_persona: Martha Johnston prefers carefully planned trips that balance intellectual enrichment and natural beauty, having explored the misty fjords of Norway, the historic streets of Edinburgh, the rice terraces of Bali, and the volcanic landscapes of Iceland, while always budgeting time for photography excursions and occasional solo retreats for meditation.
info.culinary_persona: Martha Johnston hones their culinary craft by meticulously testing Southeast Asian recipes such as pho, pad thai, and green curry, favoring ingredients like lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and fish sauce, and they proudly showcase their herb‑garden harvest of basil and cilantro in each dish, while still admitting a guilty pleasure for nightly dark chocolate with a splash of espresso.

info.persona: Daniel Jennette is a 50‑year‑old trucking‑seasoned logistics pro whose calm under pressure masks an anxious soul that fuels a passion for sunrise photography, classic rock, woodworking, and a drive to mentor new drivers while juggling impulsive gear purchases and a steadfast commitment to art‑filled weekends.
info.professional_persona: Daniel Jennette, a 50‑year‑old commercial truck driver turned regional freight sales veteran, blends 25 years of safe‑driving expertise, GPS‑driven route optimization, and client‑focused negotiation with a curious eye for contemporary art, positioning them as a calming yet emotionally reactive mentor poised to transition into a logistics coordinator or driver‑trainer role.
info.cultural_background: Daniel grew up in a small town near Dallas in a working‑class white Texan family with deep regional roots. His upbringing emphasized a strong work ethic, self‑reliance, and community involvement, reflecting mid‑century Texas culture. Raised in a Southern Baptist household, he was taught values of humility and service, though he now identifies as spiritually open. The regional culture—love of country music, high school football, barbecue, and outdoor pursuits—shapes his social life, while proximity to Dallas exposes him to a diverse arts scene that fuels his curiosity. He embraces both the rugged individualism of his Texas heritage and the broader cultural experiences he encounters through art, music, and travel.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Daniel spends his free time exploring the Texas countryside with his camera, capturing sunrise scenes over the prairie and documenting the changing urban skyline during his drives. He is a regular visitor to the Dallas Museum of Art and local galleries, where he follows contemporary exhibitions and attends artist talks. Music is another outlet; he often listens to classic rock, blues, and Texas country playlists while on the road. On weekends, he heads to Lake Ray Hubbard for fishing and occasionally joins a small woodworking club where he crafts simple furniture. Daniel also reads psychology and self‑help books to understand his anxiety, and he volunteers once a month at a community center that offers art‑therapy workshops for seniors.
info.sports_persona: Daniel Jennette enjoys weekend fishing trips on Lake Ray Hubbard as part of the local Texas Rod & Reel Association, follows the Dallas Cowboys, Dallas Mavericks, and Texas Rangers avidly, and maintains a modest fitness routine at a community gym to offset the sedentary nature of long‑haul driving.
info.arts_persona: Daniel Jennette frequents the Dallas Museum of Art, engages with contemporary exhibitions featuring artists like Mark Bradford and Kehinde Wiley, curates a personal collection of sunrise prairie photographs, and finds creative solace listening to classic rock legends such as Led Zeppelin, blues icons like B.B. King, and Texas country storytellers like Willie Nelson while on the road.
info.travel_persona: Daniel Jennette plans road trips with a blend of spontaneous GPS‑guided detours and modest pre‑trip research, favoring the wide‑open Texas prairie, weekend getaways to New Mexico’s Santa Fe, Colorado’s Rocky Mountain National Park, and occasional pilgrimages to art‑rich cities like Austin and Marfa, balancing a love for sunrise photography with a limited budget for longer vacations.
info.culinary_persona: Daniel Jennette, an amateur grill master, relishes Texas‑style brisket, smoked ribs, and fresh catfish caught at Lake Ray Hubbard, often seasoning meals with smoked paprika and cumin while whipping up easy breakfast tacos with brisket‑leftovers, and occasionally experiments with shrimp gumbo despite a tendency to over‑salt.
